name: National Landscapes
description: The 46 National Landscapes (formerly known as Areas of Outstanding Natural Beauty) across England, Wales, and Northern Ireland — protected countryside recognised for exceptional natural beauty, from chalk downland to island coastlines.

places.name: Anglesey (Ynys Môn)
places.description: An island National Landscape off North Wales, encircling almost the entire coastline with beaches, seabird colonies, and prehistoric burial chambers.

places.name: Antrim Coast & Glens
places.description: A dramatic Northern Ireland coastline of nine glens running down to the sea, with the Antrim Coast Road ranked among the world's great scenic drives.

places.name: Arnside & Silverdale
places.description: A small, coastal National Landscape straddling the Lancashire-Cumbria border, known for limestone pavement, ancient woodland, and views across Morecambe Bay's shifting sands.

places.name: Binevenagh
places.description: A striking basalt escarpment overlooking the Roe Valley and the north coast, part of the same volcanic geology as the Giant's Causeway.

places.name: Blackdown Hills
places.description: A quiet, little-visited National Landscape in Devon and Somerset, characterised by rolling hills, deep wooded combes, and traditional cider orchards.

places.name: Clwydian Range & Dee Valley
places.description: A National Landscape of rolling hills and Iron Age hillforts in northeast Wales, extended in 2011 to include the Dee Valley near Llangollen.

places.name: Cannock Chase
places.description: England's smallest National Landscape, a former royal hunting forest in Staffordshire now covered in heathland, pine forest, and mountain bike trails.

places.name: Causeway Coast
places.description: Home to the Giant's Causeway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site of hexagonal basalt columns formed by volcanic activity 60 million years ago.

places.name: Gower (Gŵyr)
places.description: The very first AONB in the UK, designated in 1956, a small Welsh peninsula famous for Rhossili Bay's sweeping sands, regularly rated among the world's best beaches.

places.name: Llŷn Peninsula
places.description: A remote Welsh peninsula stretching into the Irish Sea, its National Landscape protecting quiet coves, pilgrim history, and views to Snowdonia.

places.name: Chichester Harbour
places.description: A tidal estuary National Landscape on the Sussex-Hampshire border, a haven for sailing, wading birds, and quiet waterside villages like Bosham.

places.name: Lagan Valley
places.description: A green corridor following the River Lagan between Belfast and Lisburn, valued as accessible countryside close to Northern Ireland's largest city.

places.name: Mourne Mountains
places.description: A compact granite mountain range in County Down, said to have inspired C.S. Lewis's Narnia, ringed by the historic Mourne Wall.

places.name: Chilterns
places.description: A chalk escarpment National Landscape stretching from the Thames near Goring up through Buckinghamshire, known for beech woodlands and red kites reintroduced in the 1990s.

places.name: Cornwall
places.description: Uniquely split into 12 separate sections covering nearly a third of the county, this National Landscape protects dramatic Atlantic coastline, granite moorland, and former mining landscapes.

places.name: Ring of Gullion
places.description: A ring-shaped range of hills in County Armagh formed by an ancient volcanic ring dyke, steeped in Irish mythology tied to the legend of Cú Chulainn.

places.name: Cotswolds
places.description: The largest National Landscape in England, a belt of honey-coloured limestone hills famous for chocolate-box villages, dry-stone walls, and wool-church architecture.

places.name: Sperrin
places.description: Northern Ireland's largest upland area, a remote range of rounded hills straddling Counties Tyrone and Londonderry, historically mined for gold.

places.name: Strangford & Lecale Coast
places.description: A landscape of drumlin islands in Strangford Lough merging with the Lecale coastline, home to Mount Stewart's gardens and Game of Thrones filming locations.

places.name: Cranborne Chase
places.description: A chalk landscape straddling Dorset, Wiltshire, and Hampshire, characterised by ancient hunting-forest woodland, Bronze Age barrows, and one of England's darkest night skies.

places.name: Dedham Vale
places.description: The compact Essex-Suffolk valley immortalised in John Constable's paintings, still recognisable today from the artist's landscapes of the River Stour.

places.name: Dorset
places.description: A varied National Landscape covering chalk downland, heathland, and the Jurassic Coast's fossil-rich cliffs, stretching across much of the county.

places.name: East Devon
places.description: A coastal and rural National Landscape of red sandstone cliffs and the Jurassic Coast's eastern reaches, including the resort town of Sidmouth.

places.name: Forest of Bowland
places.description: A remote, heather-moorland National Landscape in Lancashire, historically a royal hunting ground and near the area associated with the 17th-century Pendle witch trials.

places.name: High Weald
places.description: One of the best-preserved medieval landscapes in northwest Europe, spanning Kent, Sussex, and Surrey with ancient woodland, sunken lanes, and scattered oast houses.

places.name: Howardian Hills
places.description: A gentle, wooded National Landscape in North Yorkshire between the Yorkshire Wolds and the North York Moors, dotted with historic estates like Castle Howard.

places.name: Isle of Wight
places.description: England's largest island off the Hampshire coast, its National Landscape covering chalk downs, the Needles rock stacks, and dinosaur-fossil-rich cliffs.

places.name: Isles of Scilly
places.description: England's smallest National Landscape, an archipelago 28 miles off Cornwall known for a subtropical microclimate, flower farming, and pristine white-sand beaches.

places.name: Kent Downs
places.description: A chalk ridge running from the White Cliffs of Dover to the Surrey border, nicknamed the 'Garden of England' for its orchards, hop gardens, and vineyards.

places.name: Lincolnshire Wolds
places.description: A gently rolling range of chalk hills in Lincolnshire, one of England's least-visited National Landscapes, known for wide skies and quiet villages.

places.name: Malvern Hills
places.description: A dramatic ridge of ancient volcanic rock rising abruptly from the Severn plain, long associated with composer Edward Elgar and the source of Malvern spring water.

places.name: Mendip Hills
places.description: A limestone plateau in Somerset riddled with caves and gorges, including the dramatic Cheddar Gorge, England's largest gorge.

places.name: Nidderdale
places.description: A Yorkshire Dales-adjacent National Landscape following the River Nidder, known for reservoirs, heather moorland, and the curious Brimham Rocks.

places.name: Norfolk Coast
places.description: A low-lying coastal National Landscape of salt marshes, dunes, and pine woods, home to seal colonies and some of England's best birdwatching.

places.name: North Devon
places.description: A rugged Atlantic coastline National Landscape taking in dramatic cliffs, the surf beaches around Woolacombe, and Exmoor's western fringe.

places.name: North Pennines
places.description: England's largest National Landscape, a windswept upland region of moorland and dales sometimes called 'England's last wilderness,' and a UNESCO Global Geopark.

places.name: North Wessex Downs
places.description: A chalk downland National Landscape spanning Wiltshire, Berkshire, Hampshire, and Oxfordshire, home to Avebury's prehistoric stone circle.

places.name: Northumberland Coast
places.description: A dramatic stretch of coastline dotted with castles including Bamburgh and Dunstanburgh, backed by wide sandy beaches and dune systems.

places.name: Quantock Hills
places.description: England's first ever AONB, designated in 1957, a compact range of wooded hills and heather moorland in Somerset.

places.name: Shropshire Hills
places.description: A varied upland National Landscape on the Welsh border, taking in the rocky Stiperstones, the Long Mynd moorland, and Wenlock Edge's wooded scarp.

places.name: Solway Coast
places.description: A remote, low-lying National Landscape on Cumbria's northern coast, facing Scotland across the Solway Firth, known for saltmarsh and migratory birdlife.

places.name: South Devon
places.description: A National Landscape of drowned river valleys ('rias'), fishing villages, and the South Hams' rolling countryside between Torbay and Plymouth.

places.name: Suffolk Coast & Heaths
places.description: A National Landscape of heathland, reed-fringed estuaries, and shingle beaches along the Suffolk and north Essex coast, including Sutton Hoo's Anglo-Saxon burial ground.

places.name: Surrey Hills
places.description: A wooded, chalk-and-greensand National Landscape on London's doorstep, centred on Box Hill, one of England's most-visited beauty spots.

places.name: Tamar Valley
places.description: The most recently designated English National Landscape (1995), following the river that forms the Devon-Cornwall border through former mining and market-garden country.

places.name: Wye Valley
places.description: A dramatic gorge landscape straddling England and Wales, carved by the River Wye, overlooked by the ruins of Tintern Abbey.
